reasoning: Only 480 seconds total, so I front-load everything in cycle 1 rather than scouting first and acting later. Three parallel roles: (1) 'scout' gives me the only visibility I'll have into hacking level, rooted servers, and which targets have real money — it exits fast so it costs almost nothing; (2) 'earner' is a guaranteed-to-work single-script money engine on home that starts stealing within seconds using the classic weaken/grow/hack discipline on low-level targets like n00dles and foodnstuff, which is what a fresh character can actually complete inside 8 minutes; (3) 'botnet' multiplies throughput by nuking the network and renting out every other server's RAM with a tiny 1.75GB worker, which is where most of the upside is. I deliberately split scp/exec (expensive, 3.5GB) into its own script and kept the hack/grow/weaken loop (cheap, ~2GB) separate so neither blows the 4.2GB per-script ceiling. I explicitly banned ns.getServer and ns.hackAnalyzeChance everywhere since those are the classic budget killers. Next cycle I'll use scout's report to retarget 'earner' at the highest max-money server we can actually hack, and consider a fourth agent for purchased servers if money crosses the threshold.

instruction.task: Write ONE short-lived diagnostic script that prints a compact recon report and then exits (do not loop forever). It must: (1) breadth-first scan the network from 'home' out to depth 3 collecting every hostname; (2) for each hostname print one line of comma-separated values: hostname, hasRootAccess, requiredHackingLevel, numPortsRequired, maxMoney, currentMoney, minSecurity, currentSecurity, maxRam, usedRam; (3) print the player's current hacking level and home's max/used RAM. Print with ns.tprint AND ns.print so output shows up in stdout. Finish in under ~10 seconds.
instruction.context: We are 8 minutes into a fixed 8-minute money-maximization run of Bitburner. I am the orchestrator and I am blind — I only see what your script prints. I need this recon report FAST so I can direct other agents at the most profitable targets. Runtime: export async function main(ns){...}. Static RAM budget per script is ~4.2GB. Use ONLY cheap calls: ns.scan (0.2), ns.getServerRequiredHackingLevel, ns.getServerNumPortsRequired, ns.getServerMaxMoney, ns.getServerMoneyAvailable, ns.getServerMinSecurityLevel, ns.getServerSecurityLevel, ns.getServerMaxRam, ns.getServerUsedRam, ns.hasRootAccess, ns.getHackingLevel (each ~0.05-0.1GB). ABSOLUTELY DO NOT use ns.getServer (2GB) or ns.hackAnalyzeChance (1GB) or ns.scan-based recursion without a visited Set. Guard every call in try/catch so one bad hostname cannot abort the report. await ns.sleep(0) occasionally inside loops.

instruction.task: Write ONE long-running script that immediately starts making money and never exits. Logic: maintain a hardcoded candidate target list ['n00dles','foodnstuff','sigma-cosmetics','joesguns','hong-fang-tea','harakiri-sushi','nectar-net','zer0'] . On startup, for each candidate: if not rooted, try ns.nuke (wrapped in try/catch; also try ns.brutessh/ns.ftpcrack first inside try/catch in case we own those programs). Keep only candidates that are rooted AND whose required hacking level <= ns.getHackingLevel(). Then run an infinite loop over the rooted targets executing the standard HWGW discipline per target, sequentially: if security > minSecurity + 3 -> await ns.weaken(t); else if money < 0.75 * maxMoney -> await ns.grow(t); else -> await ns.hack(t). Re-check ns.getHackingLevel() every few iterations and re-attempt nuke on candidates that were previously out of reach. Every ~15 iterations ns.print a one-line status: total money stolen so far and current player money.
instruction.context: We are in a fixed 8-minute Bitburner run starting at $1262 with a fresh low-level character. This script is the primary money engine and must start earning within seconds — favor working-now over clever. Runtime: export async function main(ns){...}. Static RAM budget per script is ~4.2GB; ns.hack/ns.grow/ns.weaken are ~0.1-0.15GB each so this fits easily. DO NOT use ns.getServer (2GB) or ns.hackAnalyzeChance (1GB) or ns.exec/ns.scp in this script. Use ns.disableLog('ALL') to keep logs clean. Wrap every hack/grow/weaken in try/catch so a single failing target never kills the loop. There must be an await inside every loop. Prefer low-level targets like n00dles and foodnstuff early since hacking skill is tiny — a fast small hack beats a long one that never completes in 8 minutes.

instruction.task: Write ONE long-running deployer script that turns every reachable server into a worker. Steps: (1) BFS scan the whole network from 'home' with a visited Set. (2) For each server without root, try ns.brutessh/ns.ftpcrack/ns.relaysmtp/ns.httpworm/ns.sqlinject each in its own try/catch (they may not exist yet), then try ns.nuke in a try/catch. (3) For every server you now have root on that has maxRam > 0, use ns.scp to copy a tiny worker file to it and ns.exec that worker with threads = floor((maxRam - usedRam) / ramCostOfWorker) (assume the worker costs 1.75GB; skip the server if threads < 1), passing the chosen target hostname as an argument. (4) Loop forever with await ns.sleep(10000), re-scanning and re-deploying to newly-rooted or idle servers, and re-attempting nuke as hacking level rises. Target selection: hardcode 'n00dles' as the default target, but if ns.getHackingLevel() is high enough for 'foodnstuff'/'joesguns' and their max money is larger, switch. The worker file itself must be created by this script via ns.write to a path like '/w.js' on home BEFORE scp; its contents are a string containing: export async function main(ns){const t=ns.args[0];while(true){try{if(ns.getServerSecurityLevel(t)>ns.getServerMinSecurityLevel(t)+3){await ns.weaken(t)}else if(ns.getServerMoneyAvailable(t)<ns.getServerMaxMoney(t)*0.75){await ns.grow(t)}else{await ns.hack(t)}}catch(e){await ns.sleep(200)}}}. ns.print a summary each cycle: how many servers rooted, how many workers launched, total threads.
instruction.context: We are in a fixed 8-minute Bitburner run. This script multiplies our earning power by using other servers' RAM; the 'earner' agent is separately hacking from home, so do not duplicate that. Runtime: export async function main(ns){...}. CRITICAL RAM BUDGET: this script's own static cost is ~4.2GB max. ns.scp + ns.exec together already cost ~3.5GB including the 1.6GB base, so you have roughly 0.7GB left — use ONLY ns.scan, ns.nuke, ns.hasRootAccess, ns.getServerMaxRam, ns.getServerUsedRam, ns.getHackingLevel, ns.write, ns.sleep on top of scp/exec, and call the port openers only via a dynamic lookup that does not add static cost if possible; if including all five port openers pushes you over budget, drop relaysmtp/httpworm/sqlinject and keep only brutessh/ftpcrack. ABSOLUTELY DO NOT use ns.getServer, ns.hackAnalyzeChance, ns.getServerMaxMoney, or ns.getServerMoneyAvailable in THIS script if RAM is tight — the worker file is a plain string and its calls cost you nothing. If ns.exec returns 0 that means RAM budget exceeded or file missing; ns.print the failure and continue rather than crashing.

reasoning: Cycle 2 of a 480s run with only $1262 — the three subagents exist but have no committed scripts yet, so the top priority is getting money-generating code live in this cycle rather than planning. I split the work along non-overlapping resource boundaries so the agents cannot fight each other: earner owns home RAM (fast, dumb, always-on weaken/grow/hack loop = immediate income), botnet owns every other server (nuke everything with 0 port requirements, self-write the worker via ns.write to avoid needing a second committed file, then fill all remaining RAM with threads = the real scaling lever), and scout runs a short-lived recon script to hand back a target list and total-RAM figure so I can retarget both workers next cycle. Every instruction carries an explicit RAM budget warning banning ns.getServer (2GB) and ns.hackAnalyzeChance (1GB), since a script that exceeds budget silently returns 0 and earns nothing — that is the main failure mode I must route around. I deliberately did not spawn a server-purchasing agent: at $1262 we cannot afford a purchased server, and I would rather revisit that once the botnet's income shows up in the next snapshot.

instruction.task: Build the botnet: a long-running deployer script that repeatedly (1) discovers every server via recursive ns.scan from home, (2) gains root on everything it can, and (3) fills every rooted server's RAM with hacking worker threads. Details: (A) At startup, build the worker source as a string in your deployer and write it to disk with ns.write('/w.js', src, 'w') — ns.write is free, so you do not need a second committed file. The worker must take the target hostname as ns.args[0] and loop forever: if security > min+5 -> await ns.weaken(target); else if money < 0.7*maxMoney -> await ns.grow(target); else -> await ns.hack(target). Worker may ONLY use ns.hack/ns.grow/ns.weaken and the cheap getters, so its per-thread RAM stays tiny (~1.75GB). (B) For root: wrap each of ns.brutessh/ns.ftpcrack/ns.relaysmtp/ns.httpworm/ns.sqlinject in try/catch (we probably own none of them yet, so failures are expected and must not crash the loop), then try/catch ns.nuke. Servers needing 0 ports (n00dles, foodnstuff, sigma-cosmetics, joesguns, hong-fang-tea, harakiri-sushi, nectar-net, zer0, CSEC, max-hardware, neo-net, iron-gym) will succeed immediately. (C) For each rooted server with maxRam > 0 (skip 'home' — another agent owns home RAM), ns.scp('/w.js', host), compute threads = floor((maxRam - usedRam) / 1.75), and if threads >= 1 ns.exec('/w.js', host, threads, target). (D) Pick target = the rooted server with the highest maxMoney whose requiredHackingLevel <= ns.getHackingLevel(); default to 'n00dles' if nothing qualifies. (E) Then loop forever with await ns.sleep(15000), re-scanning and re-deploying to newly rooted or idle servers, and re-evaluating the best target as our hacking level rises. Log each successful nuke and exec so I can see progress in stdout.
instruction.context: We are 90s into a 480s run; $1262 total. Botnet thread count is our single biggest lever on money — every idle GB on a hacked server is wasted income.
